title: Wiring contract
description: A project's own integration conventions, DERIVED from its majority behaviour and regenerated rather than hand-edited. Enforced by check_wiring_contract.py; drafted by /mycelium:wiring-contract. Guards the built-but-not-wired class: a mechanism that ships and is never called passes tests, coverage, lint and review, because each of those verifies a thing against itself while wiring is a property of a pair.

contracts.description: Rules. An EMPTY array is valid and meaningful: it records that no majority convention was detected, which is a finding rather than a pass.

pattern.description: Glob, relative to repo root, selecting the files this rule governs.

obliges.description: What a governed file must satisfy. Exactly two obligation types exist by design — nine specific obligations rot, two general ones that always run do not.

referenced_by.description: At least one file matching one of these globs must reference this file from NON-COMMENT code — by import, invocation, path, or a glob that matches it. Prose naming a file is not a call site.

sibling_reference.description: A file with this name in the SAME directory must reference it (barrel export, __init__.py, registry).

detected_from.description: The evidence that produced this rule, e.g. '18 of 20 files already satisfy this'. REQUIRED: a rule asserted without observed support is a preference, not a contract, and the next reader cannot tell the difference without this line.

confidence.description: Fraction of the governed group already satisfying the obligation when detected.

exemptions.description: Files this rule does not apply to. Each needs a REASON about the file's purpose — 'it is hard to check' is not one, since that is the false green being caught.
